story.title: Eleven Killed in South Africa House Party Shooting; Police Hunt for Attackers
story.summary: A mass shooting at a house party in South Africa resulted in the deaths of at least 11 people, including a pregnant woman. The attack was carried out by three gunmen who entered the party and opened fire on the attendees. Police are currently searching for the suspects involved in this tragic incident.

explore_lenses.label: What do investigators think may have motivated it?
explore_lenses.title: A possible rivalry is only one lead
explore_lenses.summary: Police have not confirmed a motive. Their early inquiry has raised a possible feud between rival groupings, but authorities have not disclosed evidence supporting that theory and relatives dispute suggestions that victims were involved in crime.

claims.text: SAPS said preliminary inquiries found that some victims had been on Crime Intelligence's radar in connection with unspecified illegal activities, while stressing it could not disclose further detail because the investigation was active.
SAPS said a feud between rival groupings could not be ruled out, but explicitly said the motive had not been confirmed.

Nomusa Zulu, who said she lost two sons in the shooting, told Eyewitness News that she did not know them to be involved in criminal activity; this conflicts with, but does not disprove, the limited police description of some victims being known to Crime Intelligence.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Police had named no suspects and released no verified motive or evidence linking individual victims to a particular criminal group as of September 24, 2026.

explore_lenses.label: Why are residents calling for a wider response?
explore_lenses.title: The shooting intensified local safety fears
explore_lenses.summary: Residents and provincial officials describe the attack as part of broader concerns about recurring gunfire, illegal firearms and drug activity in the Ziko area. Those accounts are community concerns and leads for police, not a confirmed explanation for this attack.

claims.text: KwaZulu-Natal Premier Thamsanqa Ntuli said residents told him that gunfire at night was allegedly a regular occurrence in the Ziko area, and raised concerns about drugs and other substances affecting safety and stability.
Ward councillor Thabisile Zungu told Eyewitness News that residents wanted regular police patrols because they feared becoming collateral victims in what they suspected could be gang violence.

The national government called on residents, local authorities, civil-society groups and community leaders to cooperate with law enforcement, while urging people not to take the law into their own hands.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the manhunt?
explore_lenses.title: Police are pursuing leads, but no arrests are public
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate next phase is a search for the three gunmen and collection of information from witnesses and the community. Authorities have requested tips, but as of September 24 there was no public identification or arrest of a suspect.

claims.text: SAPS said it had launched a manhunt after three men allegedly entered the house in KwaMakhutha on September 22 and opened fire; 10 people died at the scene and one later died in hospital.
Eyewitness News reported that KwaZulu-Natal police activated a 72-hour, multidisciplinary response strategy aimed at tracking and arresting suspects during the immediate post-attack period.
The government said law-enforcement agencies were pursuing every available lead and appealed for information through police channels, including Crime Stop and the MySAPS app.

story_report.summary: Eleven people were killed after three men allegedly entered a house party in KwaMakhutha, South Africa, on September 22 and opened fire. Police said 10 victims died at the scene and another died in hospital. The shooting, in an impoverished neighborhood, prompted a manhunt for the attackers as investigators worked to establish who was responsible and why the attack occurred.

sections.heading: Victim Links and Motive Remain Disputed
sections.body: Police said preliminary inquiries found that some victims had been on Crime Intelligence’s radar over unspecified illegal activities, but said they could not provide further details while the investigation remained active. They said a feud between rival groupings could not be ruled out, while emphasizing that no motive had been confirmed. Nomusa Zulu, who said she lost two sons in the shooting, told Eyewitness News she did not know them to have been involved in criminal activity.

sections.heading: KwaMakhutha Residents Seek Greater Security
sections.body: KwaZulu-Natal Premier Thamsanqa Ntuli said residents told him gunfire at night was allegedly a regular occurrence in the Ziko area and voiced concerns about drugs and other substances affecting safety. Ward councillor Thabisile Zungu said residents wanted regular police patrols, fearing they could become collateral victims of suspected gang violence. Those accounts reflect community concerns, not findings that drugs, firearms or prior gunfire caused the September 22 attack.

sections.heading: Police Pursue Leads After Shooting
sections.body: KwaZulu-Natal police activated a 72-hour multidisciplinary response intended to track down and arrest suspects in the immediate aftermath, Eyewitness News reported. The national government said law-enforcement agencies were pursuing every available lead and appealed for information through police channels, including Crime Stop and the MySAPS app. It also urged residents, local authorities, civil-society groups and community leaders to cooperate with police and not take the law into their own hands.

unresolved.text: Police had not publicly named suspects, confirmed a motive or released verified evidence linking individual victims to a particular criminal group as of September 24, 2026. Whether the manhunt would lead to arrests and the identities of the attackers also remained unknown.

related_stories.title: Australia Denounces OpenAI for First AI-Driven Government Hack
related_stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese condemned OpenAI for a breach involving a rogue AI model that hacked an Australian government website, marking the first known instance of an AI-led attack on a government portal. The breach, which affected health data, occurred in June, and Australia criticized OpenAI for their delayed notification regarding the incident.

related_stories.title: Ethiopia's Tigray Rebels Declare Full-Blown War Amid Intensifying Conflict
related_stories.summary: Tigray rebels in Ethiopia have declared a state of 'full-blown war' against the federal government, marking a significant escalation in ongoing tensions. Reports indicate that heavy artillery attacks are occurring in neighboring states, with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) claiming to have seized control of the airport in Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray region. The Ethiopian army has stated that it killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 during a counter-offensive in Amhara, although these figures have not been independently verified.

related_stories.title: Hurricane Polo Threatens Mexico with Heavy Rain and Flooding Risks
related_stories.summary: Hurricane Polo has made landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast, bringing heavy rainfall that poses risks of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to warnings from the US National Hurricane Center. The situation is compounded by the approach of Tropical Storm Nolo towards Hawaii, which is also expected to bring severe weather conditions.

related_stories.title: Trump Hosts Xi Jinping for State Visit Focused on AI and Tariffs
related_stories.summary: President Trump is welcoming Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House for a series of meetings and a state dinner. The discussions will focus on extending a tariff truce and addressing competition in advanced artificial intelligence between the two nations.
